result.summary: This Outsourcing Agreement governs the licensing and support of E.piphany software applications to High Speed Net Solutions, Inc. (HSNS). The contract generally protects the vendor's IP, disclaims consequential damages, and sets clear payment terms, aligning well with the Vendor Commercial Shield playbook.

categoryScores.comment: R-V-LIAB-01 Pass: The vendor's liability is capped at the total payments made under the initial term of the agreement, which satisfies the playbook requirements.
R-V-INDEM-01 Partial: The contract includes customer indemnification and vendor IP defense options, but contains broad obligations without fully mirrored protections.
R-V-TERM-01 Partial: The renewal requires mutual written agreement rather than automatic renewal with a notice period, which deviates slightly from the target.
R-V-IP-01 Pass: The vendor retains all right, title, and interest in the software and modifications, matching the playbook target.
R-V-PAY-01 Pass: Payment terms are set to Net 30, perfectly matching the playbook requirements.

redlines.originalText: HSNS hereby agrees to indemnify, defend and hold harmless E.piphany, and its officers, directors and partners (each, an "Indemnified Party") against any and all claims, demands, causes of action, damages, costs, expenses, penalties, losses and liabilities
redlines.proposedText: Each party shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the other party from and against third-party claims arising from the indemnifying party's material breach of this Agreement or infringement of third-party intellectual property rights.

chainOfThought.opposingCounselStance: E.piphany will argue that as the core technology provider, it cannot shoulder broad liabilities for third-party services and customer-facing operations managed exclusively by HSNS.
chainOfThought.commercialRiskAssessment: Unilateral indemnification exposes HSNS to open-ended liability without protection against potential IP claims originating from the core software.
chainOfThought.legalRationale: A mutual indemnification structure properly allocates risk based on fault and provides essential protection for both parties.
chainOfThought.negotiationTalkingPoint: We can agree to carve out specific operational risks if E.piphany provides a reciprocal indemnity for third-party IP infringement of the Application.

redlines.originalText: All payments made by HSNS to E.piphany hereunder are non-refundable.
redlines.proposedText: All payments made by HSNS to E.piphany hereunder are non-refundable, except that upon termination by HSNS for E.piphany's material breach or intellectual property infringement, E.piphany shall refund any prepaid unearned fees.

chainOfThought.opposingCounselStance: E.piphany will insist that prepaid subscription and license fees must remain non-refundable to maintain revenue predictability and cover upfront delivery costs.
chainOfThought.commercialRiskAssessment: Making all fees strictly non-refundable leaves HSNS financially vulnerable if E.piphany materially breaches or delivers infringing software.
chainOfThought.legalRationale: Standard commercial practice allows for refunds of prepaid, unearned fees in the event of a provider's material breach.
chainOfThought.negotiationTalkingPoint: We can accept a strict non-refundable policy for convenience terminations, provided we receive refunds upon a termination for cause.

redlines.originalText: This Agreement shall continue for a term set forth in Exhibit B, and may be renewed for successive one (1) year terms pursuant to mutual written agreement of the parties
redlines.proposedText: This Agreement shall continue for a term set forth in Exhibit B, and shall automatically renew for successive one (1) year terms unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal at least thirty (30) days prior to the end of the then-current term.

chainOfThought.opposingCounselStance: E.piphany will argue that mutual consent protects both parties from being locked into stale pricing or unwanted service extensions.
chainOfThought.commercialRiskAssessment: Requiring affirmative mutual written agreement creates administrative friction and risks accidental service interruption.
chainOfThought.legalRationale: An auto-renewal mechanism with an opt-out notice provides operational continuity while protecting both parties' right to terminate.
chainOfThought.negotiationTalkingPoint: We can agree to a 60-day notice period for non-renewal if E.piphany prefers more runway before renewals take effect.

redlines.originalText: HSNS hereby assigns all right, title and interest in and to any customization, enhancement, amendment or changes made by or for HSNS pursuant to this Agreement
redlines.proposedText: HSNS hereby assigns all right, title and interest in and to custom modifications developed specifically for E.piphany, provided that E.piphany grants HSNS a perpetual license to use such modifications in connection with the Application.

chainOfThought.opposingCounselStance: E.piphany will maintain that platform integrity and intellectual property control require all modifications to vest in the core software owner.
chainOfThought.commercialRiskAssessment: Assigning all customizations without retaining use rights could restrict HSNS's ability to service its customers effectively.
chainOfThought.legalRationale: Balancing IP ownership with a broad license to use modifications preserves core platform integrity while protecting user operations.
chainOfThought.negotiationTalkingPoint: We can agree to vest ownership in E.piphany as long as our license to use the customized functionality is explicitly secured.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: HSNS hereby agrees to indemnify, defend and hold harmless E.piphany, and its officers, directors and partners against any and all claims, demands, causes of action, damages, costs, expenses, penalties, losses and liabilities incurred by an Indemnified Party.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: Indemnification — Market Mutual IP & Third-Party Indemnification
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: (a) Provider Indemnification. Provider shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer... (b) Customer Indemnification. Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Provider... (c) Procedure.
deviations: The indemnification is primarily unilateral in favor of E.piphany.
Lacks detailed procedural requirements for notice and control of defense.
missingProtections: Mutual IP infringement indemnification from the provider.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Revise the indemnification clause to be mutual, including specific third-party IP infringement protections for the customer.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: 3.1, 3.4, 4.3, 6.2, 6.4, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13 and 14 shall survive any termination or expiration of this Agreement.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: Provisions which by their nature should survive termination, including confidentiality, indemnification, limitation of liability, payment of accrued fees, data return and deletion, and governing law, survive the expiry or termination of this Agreement.
deviations: Lists specific section numbers instead of standard categories of provisions.
missingProtections: Explicit blanket survival for provisions that by their nature should survive.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Ensure all crucial sections such as confidentiality and indemnification are explicitly listed for survival upon termination.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: THIS ALLOCATION TO WHICH THE PARTIES HAVE AGREED. THIS LIMITATION OF LIABILITY APPLIES NOTWITHSTANDING ANY FAILURE OF THE ESSENTIAL PURPOSE OF THE EXCLUSIVE REMEDIES.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: Limitation of Liability — 12-Month Trailing Aggregate Fee Cap with Balanced Super-Cap
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: (a) Consequential Damages Waiver... (b) General Aggregate Cap... (c) Super-Cap for Data Protection Breaches...
deviations: Excerpts lack explicit mention of a 12-month trailing fee cap or super-cap for data breaches.
missingProtections: Specific aggregate fee cap and heightened liability caps for data security breaches.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Add a standard 12-month trailing fee cap and a clear consequential damages waiver.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: HSNS acknowledges that E.piphany retains all right, title and interest in the Application and any modifications thereto...
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: IP Rights — Customer Work Product Ownership & Non-Use of Customer Data for AI Training
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: (a) Work Product... (b) Customer Data & AI Model Boundaries... (c) Feedback License...
deviations: Assigns custom modifications directly to E.piphany rather than reserving custom deliverables for the customer.
missingProtections: Restrictions on using customer data for AI model training.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Clarify ownership of custom work products and explicitly prohibit the use of customer data for AI training.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: For any breach of the warranties contained in Section 4.1, HSNS's sole and exclusive remedy, and E.piphany's entire liability, shall be to correct the nonconforming Application or replace defective media.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: Warranties — Performance Warranty with Re-Performance Remedy
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: The Provider warrants that (a) the Services will perform materially... (b) Services will be performed... (c) it will not knowingly introduce malicious code.
deviations: Remedies focus on correction or replacement rather than re-performance with termination rights for uncorrected breaches.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Include a robust performance warranty with standard re-performance and refund remedies.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: HSNS acknowledges that E.piphany retains all right, title and interest in the Application and any modifications thereto...
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: IP Ownership — Each Party Keeps Its Pre-Existing IP; Licence to Deliverables
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: Each party retains all rights in its intellectual property existing before or developed independently of this Agreement. The Customer owns all deliverables created specifically for it upon payment.
deviations: Contract assigns enhancements and customizations to the vendor instead of the customer owning custom deliverables.
missingProtections: Explicit retention of pre-existing IP by both parties and customer ownership of custom deliverables.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Modify IP ownership terms to ensure each party retains pre-existing IP and the customer owns custom work products.

opposingFindings.quote: HSNS hereby agrees to indemnify, defend and hold harmless E.piphany, and its officers, directors and partners (each, an "Indemnified Party") against any and all claims, demands, causes of action, damages, costs, expenses, penalties, losses and liabilities
opposingFindings.issue: The general indemnity is heavily one-sided, requiring HSNS to indemnify E.piphany without a reciprocal indemnity from E.piphany for its own breaches or IP infringement, violating standard risk allocation.
opposingFindings.leverage: E.piphany will argue that as the core technology provider, it cannot shoulder broad liabilities for third-party services and customer-facing operations managed exclusively by HSNS.

opposingFindings.quote: All payments made by HSNS to E.piphany hereunder are non-refundable.
opposingFindings.issue: Stating that all payments are completely non-refundable without carve-outs for termination due to E.piphany's material breach or intellectual property infringement creates an unfair financial risk for HSNS.
opposingFindings.leverage: E.piphany will insist that prepaid subscription and license fees must remain non-refundable to maintain revenue predictability and cover upfront delivery costs.

opposingFindings.quote: This Agreement shall continue for a term set forth in Exhibit B, and may be renewed for successive one (1) year terms pursuant to mutual written agreement of the parties
opposingFindings.issue: Requiring mutual written agreement for renewal creates operational friction and uncertainty regarding continued service availability after the initial term.
opposingFindings.leverage: E.piphany will argue that mutual consent protects both parties from being locked into stale pricing or unwanted service extensions.

opposingFindings.quote: HSNS hereby assigns all right, title and interest in and to any customization, enhancement, amendment or changes made by or for HSNS pursuant to this Agreement
opposingFindings.issue: Forcing HSNS to assign all rights in customizations and enhancements without retaining a broad license to use them independently could restrict HSNS's operational flexibility.
opposingFindings.leverage: E.piphany will maintain that platform integrity and intellectual property control require all modifications to vest in the core software owner.
